newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UN condemns Iraq for "all-pervasive repression".
newsitem.headline: UN condemns Iraq for "all-pervasive repression".

text.p: The U.N. Human Rights Commission, in one of its strongest resolutions on any country this year, accused Iraq on Wednesday of "all-pervasive repression" including systematic torture, widespread terror and killings.

In a resolution adopted by 31 votes to nil with 22 abstentions, mainly from developing countries, the world's supreme body for human rights protection accused Baghdad of "massive and extremely grave" human rights abuses.
These resulted in "an all-pervasive repression and oppression sustained by broad-based discrimination and widespread terror", the resolution said.
The 53-member Commission, of which Iraq is not a member, strongly condemned president Saddam Hussein's government for its summary and arbitrary executions and arbitrary arrests.
It accused Iraq's government of "widespread, systematic torture in its most cruel forms" and extended the mandate of the U.N. human rights investigator for the country for another year.
It also urged Iraq to resolve the cases of Kuwaitis and other foreigners missing since Saddam's invasion of Kuwait in 1990.
